messages:
Maria (PM): kicking off PRD handoff for the Optimize recommendations (batching / cache / quantization). Need clear launch gates + acceptance criteria. @Akshay can you confirm the customer asks we need to bake into acceptance?
Akshay (ML Eng): TL;DR: two big customer asks — (1) low-latency customers want quantized model option with quality within ~1% of FP baseline; (2) cost-first customers want aggressive batching + cache reuse even if p95 increases a bit. Details below.
Akshay (ML Eng): paste notes: 
```
Customer A (finance): latency p50 < 70ms, p95 < 180ms, quality delta <= 1% (EM, rouge sim) with int8/qlora.
Customer B (search): target cost reduction 40% vs current baseline, throughput >= 3x at peak, can accept p95 up to 400ms.
```
Tom (Eng): got it. For PRD we need exact metrics hooks + automated checks. Suggest these acceptance tests: perf harness run (short/long seq), quality regression eval on 3 eval sets, and cache consistency tests.
Jordan (Eng-Platform): rollout plan request: canary to 5% traffic with synchronous fallback to FP model, automatic rollback on quality/regression alert. Need config knobs: canary_percent, fallback_model, max_cache_ttl.
Lucas (ProdOps): make sure observability includes token-level cost, batch-size histogram, KV-cache hit ratio, and trace id passthrough. We should have alerts: cache-thr drops by >10% or p95 increases >20% in 10m window.
Sara (Head of Product): proposed launch gates (rough):
- Gate 1: Implementation & unit tests complete
- Gate 2: Internal perf and quality pass (no regressions on core evals)
- Gate 3: Canary w/ rollback + monitoring dashboards in Console
- Gate 4: Customer pilot sign-off (Customer A or B)
Maria (PM): mapping acceptance criteria to gates:
- Gate 2 acceptance: baseline evals show quality delta <= 1% and throughput targets met in lab (batching profile included).
- Gate 3 acceptance: canary run 48h w/o rollback, KV-cache hit >= 60% for cache-enabled routes, no more than 1% error rate increase.
Akshay (ML Eng): edge cases we flagged: short prompts (<= 32 tokens) where batching hurts tail latency, long context (>= 4k) where quantized kernels may OOM on some GPUs, and cache invalidation for streamed completions. Need explicit tests for each.
Tom (Eng): agree. I'll add small perf test commands to repo: 
```
# run perf harness
python perf/run.py --model candidate --seq-lens 16,512,2048 --batch-sizes 1,8,32 --measure p50,p95
```
Jordan (Eng-Platform): add rollout policy: default to conservative batching for latency-tier customers; policy config example: `{"latency_slo_ms": 120, "prefer_quant": false}`. We'll expose via Console for customers.
Lucas (ProdOps): also require an incident playbook snippet in PRD: steps to revert to FP model, how to clear KV-cache safely, who to pager.
ci-bot: CI: perf-harness job queued for branch optimize/prd-acceptance (job #342).
Maria (PM): sign-offs needed: @Sara for product acceptance, @Akshay for ML quality, @Tom & @Jordan for infra/rollout, @Lucas for ops readiness. Can everyone reply with :thumbsup: and ETA for sign-off?
Akshay (ML Eng): :thumbsup: ETA EOD Wednesday. Need a final eval run after latest quant kernels.
Tom (Eng): :thumbsup: ETA Thu morning. Will add harness scripts + unit tests.
Jordan (Eng-Platform): :thumbsup: ETA Thu afternoon. Will wire rollout flags and dashboard links.
Lucas (ProdOps): :thumbsup: ETA Fri. I'll draft playbook and alert thresholds.
Sara (Head of Product): :thumbsup: ETA Fri noon. Will coordinate customer pilot invites.
Maria (PM): great — I'll update the PRD with the gates & acceptance criteria and add a short checklist for the on-call and pilot. Leaving a note: prioritize short-prompt latency experiments first; caching behaviour there will determine default policies.
Akshay (ML Eng): one more edge-case: quantized model + KV-cache cross-version mismatch — we should invalidate cache on model-version change by default. Add to PRD.
Tom (Eng): agreed. Also add test: replay old cached keys against new model to verify no silent quality shifts.
Maria (PM): thanks all. I'll push the PRD update and tag reviewers. If you have follow-ups drop them here. :rocket:
